items.title: 4.4 Molar mass and density of gases

source_refs.note: Topic 4.4, printed page 80; Sample Problem 4.9 and Quick Check 4.3 as the self-check.

blocks.title: Density
blocks.text: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance: d = m / V.

Since one molar mass of every gas occupies the same volume at STP, the density of a gas depends on its molar mass: a gas of higher molar mass has higher density and vice versa. If the density of a gas at STP is measured, its molar mass can be calculated as mass = density x volume, taking the volume of one mole as 22.4 dm3. Sample Problem 4.9: a gas of density 1.97 g/dm3 at STP has molar mass 1.97 x 22.4 = 44.1 g/mol.

blocks.prompt: Calculate the molar mass of a gas whose density at STP is 1.34 g/dm3, and of another whose density is 1.43 g/dm3. Which common gases could they be?
blocks.explanation: 1.34 x 22.4 = 30.0 g/mol, which matches ethane (C2H6) or nitric oxide (NO). 1.43 x 22.4 = 32.0 g/mol, which matches oxygen, O2.

items: Density d = m / V; at STP every gas has one mole in 22.4 dm3, so molar mass = density x 22.4 (1.97 g/dm3 gives 44.1 g/mol).
